newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya extends voter registration exercise again.
newsitem.headline: Kenya extends voter registration exercise again.

text.p: Kenya's National Electoral Commission (NEC) on Tuesday extended voter registration for the second time this week, by six days, privately-owned Kenya Television Network reported.
Quoting an NEC statement, the network said registration had been extended to June 30 to allow thousands of Kenyans who had not yet registered to do so for elections due later this year.
On Monday the commission extended voter registration by two days from the original deadline of June 22.
Residents across the East African country have complained that the process is slow and inefficient.
Member of parliament Paul Muite complained on Tuesday that many young men and women in his Kikuyu constituency had been turned away and refused to register as voters.
"I suggest that voter registration should be extended by a fortnight," Muite wrote to the NEC chairman earlier on Tuesday.

The commission said on Monday it had registered only six million voters in the country of nearly 30 million people. This is fewer than those registered in the last polls in 1992 and far below the current potential electorate of 10 million.
President Daniel arap Moi, 73, is favourite to extend his 19-year rule for five more years because of existing electoral rules and deep personal and ethnic splits within the opposition.
